speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly when the bleeding started after your wisdom tooth extraction and whether it has stopped at any point since then? Also, have you noticed easy bruising elsewhere on your body or a history of prolonged bleeding from minor cuts?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of bleeding from your gums, nose, or after other minor surgeries? Has anyone in your family been diagnosed with a specific bleeding disorder, such as Hemophilia or von Willebrand disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

text: Does the patient experience joint swelling or bleeding into joints without significant trauma, and has there been any bleeding after previous minor surgical procedures like circumcision? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: That prior diagnosis of gastroenteritis seems inconsistent with your current presentation of post-extraction bleeding and a family history suggestive of a coagulation disorder. I need to clarify if you have experienced bleeding from your gums, nose, or after minor cuts in the past, as this is crucial for differentiating between von Willebrand disease and hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX Activity Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, we can rule out Hemophilia A and B, so let's focus on von Willebrand disease given the mucosal bleeding pattern. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor VIII, IX, and von Willebrand studies, I suspect a platelet function disorder like Glanzmann thrombasthenia. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Aggregation Study

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: Since platelet aggregation is normal, I need to check for a qualitative platelet defect like dense granule deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Function Analyzer (PFA-100)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal results for all standard coagulation and platelet function tests, I need to ask if you have a personal history of hemarthrosis (bleeding into joints) or if the bleeding stops completely with prolonged pressure. This will help distinguish between a rare qualitative platelet defect and other vascular causes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis is clearly incorrect given your bleeding symptoms. Given the normal standard labs but persistent mucosal bleeding and family history of joint issues, I must consider Factor XIII deficiency, which requires specific testing.
